chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said:

A man asked him about a man who died and left two brothers and a daughter, and the daughter was young. So one of the two brothers, the executor, married the daughter to his own son. Then the father of the married son died. So when he died, the other brother said, 'My brother did not marry his son, so he married the girl to his son.' So it was said to the girl, 'Which of the two husbands is more beloved to you, the first or the last?' She said, 'The last.' Then the second brother died, and for the first brother was a son closer (older) than the son who had been given in marriage. So he said to the girl, 'Choose which of the two is more beloved to you, the first husband or the last husband?'

So he said, 'The report in it is that she is for the last husband, and that is because she had reached adulthood when she was married off, and it is not for her to break what she had bonded to after her adulthood.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a young girl is married by two different guardians and she chooses one after reaching adulthood?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the principle of *Ikhtiyar* (choice) in Shia jurisprudence, where a pre-pubescent girl married by a guardian retains the right to choose between her two concurrent marriages upon reaching maturity. The ruling underscores that the initial contract remains valid and binding once she attains the age of discretion, preventing the annulment of the first marriage simply because a second was contracted by another guardian. This case highlights the nuanced application of guardianship (*Wilayah*) and the legal capacity of the bride to validate or reject the marital bond upon her own volition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie who said,

‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died and left two brothers and the daughter, and the daughter was young. So one of the brothers was the executor of the will, so he got the daughter married to his own son. Then the father who got the son married, died. So when he died, the other brother said, ‘He did not get his son married, so he got the girl married to his own son. So it was said to the girl, which of the two husbands is more beloved to you, the former or the later?’ She said, ‘The later’. Then the second brother died, and for the first brother was son older than the son of the one who had given in marriage. So he said to the girl, ‘Choose which of the two is more beloved to you, the first husband or the last?’

So he (the narrator) said, ‘The report has in it that she is for the later husband, and that is because she had happened to have reached adulthood when she was married off, and it is not for her that she breaks what she had bonded to, after her adulthood’.[1483] (p.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il ibn Bazi’ who has said the following:

“Once a man asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind two brothers and a daughter who is small. One brother becomes the executor of the will and gives the girl in marriage to his son. The father of the boy married to the girl dies and thereafter the other brother says that his brother did not give the girl in marriage to his son so he gives the girl in marriage to his son and the girl is asked, ‘Which one of the (two) husbands is more beloved to you?’ She says, ‘The other one (son of the second brother) is more beloved to me.’ Then the second brother dies and the other brother has left behind another son older than the son who was married to the girl. He asks the girl to choose whichever of the two she likes.

He (the narrator) has said that Hadith about this case says that she is for the second husband because she at that time was able to discern when she was given in marriage and it is not lawful for her to disregard the marriage which is formed after her gaining the ability to discern.’”
